committed_before: any code for ARK006-ARK011, and before the taint-source engine change
why_this_file_exists: The v0.2 rules are being designed from the classes ARKEXA missed on the
first corpus. If the queries that collect the next corpus were chosen
after those rules were written, the corpus would be shaped by the
detection patterns and any recall figure from it would measure only that
the rules find what they were pointed at. Committing the queries first,
with a timestamp, is what makes the eventual number defensible - and it
cannot be done convincingly after the fact, which is why it is done now.

allowed: an agent name or credential string from src/arkexa/data/agents.yml
at most one trigger event per query
forbidden: any conjunction that matches a rule's structural signature
reasoning: Trigger stratification is not new: METHODOLOGY step 3 already required
it so schedule-only workflows are not over-represented. Naming a
trigger continues published method. Naming the sink, the scope or the
ref expression alongside it would be writing the answer key, because
that conjunction is exactly what ARK009 and ARK011 match on.

enriched_reason: Declared enriched even though collection is query-driven, because the
trigger balance below was chosen knowing which classes were missed.
That skew is legitimate for measuring recall and disqualifying for
prevalence. Over-declaring costs nothing; under-declaring would let a
prevalence figure be computed from a corpus that cannot support one.
score.py refuses prevalence on this corpus as a result.
exclusions: at most one workflow per repository, as before

target.draw_order: shuffled and published, so stopping partway stays representative

notes: 24 queries. Fourteen vary the trigger for agents already known to appear
in real workflows; eight cover agents in the inventory that the first
collection never queried (openhands, shell-gpt, ollama, crush,
copilot-cli, continue, sweep, openai-assistant); two are credential
strings, which catch agents invoked in ways no signature matches.
A query that returns nothing is recorded as returning nothing rather
than replaced, because silently swapping a query for a more productive
one after seeing the results is the same contamination in slower form.
